brief: Check whether a promotion’s minimum spend makes the planned purchase more expensive.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Promotion Costs"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "¿La promoción cuesta más?"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "A promoção custa mais?"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Check whether a promotion’s minimum spend makes the planned purchase more expensive.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: Spending extra to unlock a discount may raise the final bill; compare the promotion with your original plan.
instruction.misconception: Qualifying for a promotion always saves money even when unwanted extras raise spending above the original plan.
instruction.numeracy_support: Use only the visible fictional amounts and conditions; earlier arithmetic is preparation, not a hidden financial assumption.

evidence.reasoning: Calculate the qualifying basket after its discount. Compare with the planned basket; a discount can still require more spending.
The promotion costs more than the original plan.
The original plan is the relevant comparison for actual spending.
The discounted basket still exceeds the original planned spending.
Unused extras can make a promotion poor value.
Excluded products may not help reach the required threshold.
The promotion increases spending without meeting an additional stated need.

delayed_retrieval.fresh_context: Retrieve this competence in the declared later course reviews and through the existing shared review system.
